record.original_question: Is every odd positive integer greater than 5 expressible as the sum of three primes?

evidence.quote: The weak Goldbach conjecture states that every odd positive integer greater than 5 can be written as the sum of three primes. In 2013, H. A. Helfgott posted a proof that the conjecture is true.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Prove or disprove: every odd integer n > 5 can be written as a sum of three prime numbers (where the primes need not be distinct, and a prime is a positive integer p ≥ 2 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p).
artifact.status_search_result: The weak (ternary) Goldbach conjecture was proven by H. A. Helfgott in 2013, who showed every odd integer greater than 5 is the sum of three primes. The proof combines major-arc estimates, minor-arc bounds, and computational verification up to a sufficient threshold.

status_evidence.title: The ternary Goldbach conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Helfgott's proof that every odd number greater than 5 is the sum of three primes.
status_evidence.claim: Helfgott proved the weak Goldbach conjecture in 2013.
